text:
incident-bot: ALERT: GPU_PREFILL_OOM detected on hotpool-3 (node flap risk). Severity: P1. Paging oncall: @tara. Runbook: https://redwood/runbooks/prefill-oom

tara: I’m on it, joining bridge in 2. Can someone post quick customer impact summary? :phone:

aj: seeing repeated container restarts on hotpool-3. Logs show long-context prefill spikes from a single customer workload, very large prompt windows (~1.2M tokens) causing CUDA OOM during allocation.

liam: confirmed node reported: 
```
[2026-03-16T22:40:11Z] runtime: cudaMalloc failed: out of memory
[2026-03-16T22:40:11Z] prefill: alloc req 12.4GB -> triggered OOM, container restart
[2026-03-16T22:40:12Z] containerd: task exited with status 137
```

sophie: Support note: we have two customers with elevated error rates (svc-a and svc-b). svc-a traffic dropped by ~18% and we already have two tickets started. No public comms yet.

aj: mitigation plan (short):
1) Enable adaptive prefill throttle for hotpool-3 to cap prefill tokens to 256k per request.
2) Apply temporary routing rule to send long-context requests to a coldmodel fallback (lower mem footprint).
3) Evict large KV caches on impacted nodes to free VRAM.
4) If restarts continue, cordon+drain hotpool-3 and failover tasks.

aj: running commands now:
```bash
# enable throttle (runtime flag)
redwoodctl runtime set-flag --pool hotpool-3 --flag prefill_adaptive_throttle=on --max_tokens=256000
# route rule to coldmodel-fallback
redwoodctl routing create --match 'context_tokens>256000' --target coldmodel-fallback --priority 100
# kv cache eviction on node 
ssh gpu-34 'sudo systemctl restart redwood-kvcache && sudo redwoodctl kvcache evict --pool hotpool-3 --percent 90'
```

tara: ack. Do the throttle change and routing in that order. Notify me when the node is cordoned.

liam: I’m watching node metrics. After throttle + routing we see a drop in prefill allocations on hotpool-3 within 30s. Memory pressure reduced from 94% -> 64% on gpu-34.

aj: applied routing rule and throttle. Eviction triggered. Observed one additional restart immediately after, but no new restarts in the last 8 minutes.

sophie: customer update draft (internal): "We observed transient errors for long-context requests affecting svc-a and svc-b between 22:38-22:52 UTC. We applied mitigations; service is recovering. We'll follow up with a post-incident note."

mike: Product: keep me posted on potential permanent limits. Teams want guardrails to avoid noisy neighbor long-context abuse.

aj: follow-up actions:
- short-term: keep adaptive_throttle on for 4h, monitor error rate.
- mid-term: add prefill token quota per API key and a soft failure mode to suggest truncation.
- infra: add faster kvcache eviction hook and more granular per-request memory accounting.

tara: oncall handoff: I’ll stay 30m then hand to @liam if stable. If errors spike back we escalate to eng-runtime and initiate node drain plan.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigations applied by aj. Severity remains P1 while oncall monitors. Bridge: https://redwood/bridge/5222345678

liam: creating postmortem stub and linking logs. I’ll include timelines and the change to routing as the primary mitigation.

sophie: opening customer tickets and linking to the bridge notes. Will ping legal if any SLA thresholds reached. :white_check_mark:

aj: final note: we should add a regression alert for sudden increases in prefill token size per API key to catch this faster.

tara: thanks team. Keeping watch, will update handoff at +30m. :lock:
